moat_against: Moat substantially policy-conferred: 45X credits, tariffs and domestic-content adders can be legislated down
Global module pricing set by Chinese crystalline-silicon oversupply
Single product family, utility-scale only — no market diversification
Backlog shrinking at the margin (47.9 GW Q1 2026 → 45.1 GW Q2 2026); bookings pace is the swing factor
Tellurium supply constrains ultimate CdTe scale; concentrated utility-developer customer base
moat_for: Only scaled CdTe thin-film platform — differentiated, vertically integrated technology
US-integrated supply chain independent of Chinese crystalline silicon and its tariff exposure
Contracted backlog 45.1 GW / $13.6B through 2030; US capacity substantially sold out through 2028
Domestic-content requirements on ~41 GW of backlog that only FSLR fills at scale
Net-cash balance sheet — survives policy or demand downturns
moat_justification: Only scaled CdTe thin-film platform, fully US-integrated and independent of Chinese crystalline silicon, with a 45.1 GW / $13.6B contracted backlog and a net-cash balance sheet — but the largest pillar (Section 45X credits of $2.10–2.19B in the FY2026 guide, tariff protection, domestic-content adders) is conferred by policy and can be legislated away, capping the score at 6.
name: First Solar, Inc.
one_liner: Dominant US CdTe module maker, moat 6/10, net cash — but the moat is substantially policy-rented (45X) and at $178.81 the guidance-calibrated weighted IRR is 13.2% vs the 15% hurdle; it clears 15% at $151.05.
